title: Per-view timing rows extracted from STA artefacts
description: The document _ppa/timing.py emits. Its reason for existing is that a design has a timing MATRIX (mode x corner x check) and not a WNS; every row is one cell of that matrix and carries the full scope needed to compare it with another. See docs/PPA_INTERFACES.md sections 2 and 5.

allOf.description: A MEASURED row carries the number it measured.

THE NO-SENTINEL RULE, made machine-checkable. A row that is not MEASURED must carry NO value key at all -- not 0, not -1, not null. 0 and 'not measured' are different facts, and a reader that finds a number does not ask which one it was. It carries a reason instead.

EVERY ABSENT SCOPE KEY IS EXPLAINED. Omitting a key the producer could not establish is the fix for the null sentinel; omitting it SILENTLY is the same defect wearing a different spelling, because a reader still cannot tell 'this view has no RC corner axis' from 'nobody recorded one'. So for each of the eight, absent from `scope` REQUIRES a sentence under that key in `scope_gaps`. This is the machine-checkable half of the v1.11.69 producer change; `_ppa/timing._gaps_for` is the half that writes them.

scope.description: THE KEYS THIS ARTEFACT ESTABLISHED, AND NO NULLS. Until v1.11.69 this said 'all eight keys, always -- an omitted key and a null key are different claims to a reader and only one of them is true'. Both halves of that are right and the conclusion was wrong: `null == null`, so two rows that could not read their RC corner compared as rows taken at the SAME RC corner, and a head-to-head could put them side by side. MEASURED over 12 real run trees before the change: 152 rows refused SCOPE_SENTINEL. docs/PPA_INTERFACES.md section 2 has said 'a scope key that is present and null is worse than one that is absent' since v1.11.53 and `_ppa/metrics.validate` enforces it; this schema now says the same thing. A key a producer could not establish is ABSENT and its reason is REQUIRED in `scope_gaps` (see metric_row) -- an unexplained hole is the same invisible claim as a null, moved one field over. NO key is required HERE, `stage` included: this is an EXTRACTOR document and a report that stamps no basis must still be able to publish an honest row saying so. `_ppa/metrics._REQUIRED_SCOPE` is what refuses such a row (SCOPE_INCOMPLETE) when it is offered as a MEASUREMENT -- the gate is the layer that refuses, and duplicating its rule here would stop the extractor emitting the very row that makes the missing stamp visible. THE THREE PATH KEYS ARE THE ONLY PERMITTED EXTRAS, and only `timing.*.worst_path_slack_ns` carries them: that metric is emitted once per REPORTED PATH, so several rows land in one view with different slacks, and without a key naming the path they collide as one identity holding three values. `additionalProperties` stays false -- an undeclared scope key makes a record incomparable to every other record.

path_startpoint.description: Where the reported path starts. An IDENTITY: the same in two runs of one design, so two arms' rows for one path carry equal scope and stay comparable.

path_endpoint.description: Where the reported path ends. Emitted with `path_startpoint` or not at all.

path_ordinal.description: Position in the printed list, used ONLY when the artefact named no endpoints. It separates the rows inside one document but it is not an identity -- reorder the tool's output and it moves -- so a cross-arm comparison over it refuses on differing scope, which is the honest answer for a path that cannot be shown to be the same path.

stage.description: Present only when the artefact ESTABLISHED it. Never null: two nulls compare equal and would make two different facts comparable. When absent, `scope_gaps.stage` says why.
